issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Daily Check-in block wipes already-logged water and fabricates sleep/mood on submit.

The coach-chat daily_checkin block (src/components/blocks/DailyCheckinBlock.tsx) seeds water=0, sleep=7h, mood=3 from a `data.defaults` field the backend never sends (the show_daily_checkin tool schema in app/services/coach_tools.py only has `date`/`fields`/`previous_values` - no `defaults`), and handleSubmit ALWAYS includes water_ml, sleep_hours and mood in the payload. Only weight has an omit-when-untouched guard (`...(weight > 0 && {...})`).

Backend POST /logs/daily `_apply_daily_fields` (app/routes/logging.py) sets every present non-null field, so a check-in submitted without touching water overwrites the day's water_intake_liters with 0 - silently wiping water the user logged earlier via the Nutrition page - and writes sleep_hours=7 + energy_rating=6 (mood 3 x2) that the user never entered.

Compounding: the block ignores the backend's required `fields` array entirely - a coach-requested weight-only check-in still renders and submits all 4 fields.

Expected: untouched fields are omitted from the payload (same pattern as weight), and the form respects data.fields.
Actual: water zeroed, sleep/mood fabricated on every submit.

Repro: 1) Log ~2L water on /nutrition. 2) In coach chat, get a daily_checkin block (ask coach for a check-in). 3) Enter only weight, tap Submit Check-in. 4) GET /logs/daily for today: water_intake_liters is 0 and sleep_hours is 7.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: DailyCheckinBlock now tracks touched fields (Set<string>). handleSubmit only includes water_ml/sleep_hours/mood when the user has actually interacted with that field - same omit-when-untouched pattern as weight. Also respects data.fields array from backend to render only coach-requested fields. Commit 17b12af8.

judge.note: Code fix in DailyCheckinBlock.tsx: touched Set tracks user interactions; handleSubmit guards: ..(touched.has('water') && {water_ml}), ..(touched.has('sleep') && {sleep_hours}), ..(touched.has('mood') && {mood}). showField() respects data.fields. Proxy screenshot (coach chat blocks require live native session).

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Scrolling coach chat wipes in-progress interactive-block input (production only).

CoachChatMessageList virtualizes rows when VITE_COACH_CHAT_VIRTUALIZE=true - which .env.production line 24 enables (dev default is off) - with overscan: 6. TanStack Virtual UNMOUNTS rows that scroll past the overscan window, and every interactive block keeps its form state in component-local useState: WorkoutTrackerBlock set reps/weights/completed checkboxes, DailyCheckinBlock weight/water/sleep/mood, MultiSelectBlock selections, WaterLoggerBlock tapped increments. Only the completed/active status is lifted to the parent (blockStatuses in CoachChat.tsx); draft input is not.

So a user mid-workout who has checked off 3 sets and adjusted weights in a workout_tracker block, scrolls up ~7+ messages to re-read the coach's instructions, then scrolls back down, finds the tracker silently reset to its planned defaults - every checked set and edited value gone. Same for a half-filled daily check-in.

Expected: in-progress block input survives scrolling (persist draft state per blockKey outside the virtualized row, e.g. a parent-level map/ref cache alongside blockStatuses, keyed the same way).
Actual: offscreen unmount discards it.

Repro (needs prod flag): build/serve with VITE_COACH_CHAT_VIRTUALIZE=true, open a coach chat long enough to scroll, get a workout_tracker block at the bottom, check 2-3 sets WITHOUT submitting, scroll to the top of the thread, scroll back down - checked sets are cleared. Dev builds (flag off) do not reproduce, which is why QA misses it.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Thread cacheKey (= blockKey) from MessageBlockSlot through InteractiveBlock to each block. WorkoutTrackerBlock and DailyCheckinBlock use module-level Maps (_exerciseStateCache, _checkinDraftCache) keyed by cacheKey. useEffect writes state to cache on every change; useState initializer reads from cache on remount. Commit 17b12af8.

judge.note: Code fix: BlockProps.cacheKey, InteractiveBlock passes it to Component, MessageBlockSlot passes cacheKey={blockKey}. WorkoutTrackerBlock: _exerciseStateCache.get(cacheKey) in useState init + useEffect writes back. DailyCheckinBlock same pattern. Proxy screenshot (VITE_COACH_CHAT_VIRTUALIZE=true is prod-only flag).

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Weekly weigh-in reminder is wired to the WRONG preference toggle. The Sunday weigh-in local notification (REMINDER_IDS.WEIGH_IN, Android channel 'progress_updates') is scheduled and cancelled inside applyWorkoutReminders() in src/pages/NotificationPreferences.tsx (~line 79-104), so it is controlled by the "Workout Reminders" switch instead of "Progress Updates".

EXPECTED: turning OFF "Progress Updates" stops the weekly weigh-in nudge (its channel + content are progress, not workout); turning OFF "Workout Reminders" stops only workout nudges.

ACTUAL: (1) user turns OFF "Progress Updates" -> Sunday 8am weigh-in reminder still fires (it is only cancelled when workout_reminders_enabled goes false). (2) user turns OFF "Workout Reminders" but keeps "Progress Updates" ON -> weigh-in reminder is silently cancelled too. The mount-time recovery effect (~line 258-269) has the same coupling: it re-schedules WEIGH_IN whenever workout_reminders_enabled is true, even if progress_updates_enabled is false, so the wrong state self-heals back on every visit to the page.

REPRO (native build): 1) open /notification-preferences with push on, all categories on 2) toggle "Progress Updates" OFF 3) adb shell dumpsys notification (or wait until Sunday 8:00) -> pending intent id 1030 'Weekly weigh-in' still scheduled on the progress_updates channel the user just disabled.

FIX DIRECTION: schedule/cancel WEIGH_IN from the progress_updates_enabled toggle (own applyProgressReminders helper), and mirror that in the recovery effect.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Weekly weigh-in reminder was wired to workout toggle instead of progress toggle. Already fixed in f178eb35: separate applyProgressReminders() helper controls WEIGH_IN, wired to progress_updates_enabled toggle and recovery effect.

judge.note: Bug already fixed in f178eb35. Code confirmed: applyWorkoutReminders() (line 78-96) handles only REMINDER_IDS.WORKOUT. applyProgressReminders() (line 100-119) is a separate helper that exclusively handles REMINDER_IDS.WEIGH_IN and is wired to progress_updates_enabled toggle (line 242-243). Recovery effect also checks prefs.progress_updates_enabled for WEIGH_IN (line 301-302). Separation is complete and correct.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Quiet Hours are never applied to device-local reminders — the toggle's promise ("No push during sleep") only holds for server FCM push. Backend suppression works (is_in_quiet_hours() in app/services/notification_service.py gates every server send), but all local reminders scheduled via src/lib/localNotifications.ts (meal x3, workout, weigh-in) use plain LocalNotifications.schedule({on:{hour,minute}}) with no quiet-hours check, and nothing re-schedules or cancels them when the user changes quiet_hours_start/end or toggles quiet hours on /notification-preferences.

EXPECTED: with Quiet Hours enabled (e.g. 12:00-14:00 for a night-shift user, or any window overlapping a default reminder slot), no notification fires inside the window — the settings card says "No push during sleep" with no exception noted.

ACTUAL: a lunch reminder hard-coded to 13:00 (DEFAULT_REMINDER_TIMES in NotificationPreferences.tsx) fires at 13:00 even when quiet hours are 12:00-14:00. Same for breakfast 8:00 / dinner 19:00 / workout 7:00 / weigh-in Sun 8:00 vs any user-set window covering them. Editing the quiet-hours time inputs PUTs the pref to the server but triggers zero local re-scheduling (update() in NotificationPreferences.tsx only reacts to meal/workout/push toggles), so the device schedule and the stated preference silently diverge.

REPRO (native build): 1) enable Meal Reminders 2) enable Quiet Hours and set 12:00-14:00 3) wait for 13:00 -> 'Lunch time' local notification fires inside the quiet window.

FIX DIRECTION: when quiet_hours_* change (or on the mount recovery pass), skip/re-schedule local reminders whose fire time falls inside the window, or shift them to quiet_hours_end — matching the server-side suppression semantics.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Quiet hours not applied to local device reminders. Already fixed in f178eb35: quiet_hours change triggers re-schedule of all local reminders via each apply* helper; each helper checks isInQuietWindow() and cancels reminders that fall in the quiet window.

judge.note: Bug already fixed in f178eb35. Code confirmed: quiet_hours change handler (line 244-251) re-applies ALL local reminders with the new quiet config (applyMealReminders, applyWorkoutReminders, applyProgressReminders all called with updated 'quiet' param). Each apply* function calls isInQuietWindow() and cancels the reminder if it falls in the window. Device schedule is updated immediately on quiet_hours_* field change, matching server-side suppression semantics.

issues.description: [suggestion] Exercise form-cue sheet: tap any exercise in a workout to see 3-4 concise form cues, common mistakes, and a breathing tip. USER PROBLEM: during a live workout the athlete sees only exercise name + sets×reps×RPE — zero guidance on how to actually perform the movement. Beginners (the walking_only/light tiers the app explicitly provisions for) either guess (injury + bad results) or leave the workout screen to ask the coach chat / Google, which kills the session flow and burns LLM rate-limit budget on a static question. EVIDENCE: a repo-wide grep finds NO instruction/video/form-cue content anywhere — the exercise catalog carries only equipment/sets/reps/RPE (ExercisePickerSheet, getAlternatives), and Activity.tsx's live-workout card renders no info affordance. Every comparable tracker (Hevy, Strong, Fitbod, cult.fit) ships per-exercise how-to as table stakes. V1 SCOPE: an info icon on the exercise card in the live workout (Activity.tsx) and in NextSessionPreview opens a calm bottom sheet with: 3-4 form cues, 2 common mistakes, 1 breathing tip. Content is LLM-generated ONCE per exercise server-side and cached in a new exercise_form_cues table (exercise_id → JSON), served via GET /api/v1/exercises/<id>/form-cues; first-request-generates, then cached forever — so LLM cost is one call per distinct exercise ever, not per user. No video, no images, no personalization in v1. EFFORT: ~2 days full-stack (1 endpoint + 1 table + migration; 1 bottom-sheet component + 2 tap targets). Zero impact on existing flows if the endpoint 404s (sheet just doesn't open).
issues.author: shakeebshaan

issues.description: [suggestion] Live 16:8 intermittent-fasting timer on the Nutrition page. USER PROBLEM: the app already lets users flag a fasting day (Vrat / Full fast / 16:8 window) but that is a STATIC boolean banner -- it only pauses meal reminders. It does not tell the user where they are IN the fast, which is the whole point of intermittent fasting: how long have I fasted, and when does my eating window open/close? Without a live count, 16:8 is unusable and users abandon it. EVIDENCE: FastingBanner in src/pages/Nutrition.tsx (~lines 47-100) offers a '16:8 window' type but renders no timer/countdown -- a grep shows zero fasting-timer / eating-window code, so the live feature is a genuine gap, not a duplicate. Intermittent fasting is a headline retention feature in every major tracker used in India (HealthifyMe, Zero, Fastic), and vrat/fasting is already culturally central to this India audience (the app even ships a 'Vrat / fruit-only' fast type). V1 SCOPE: when the user picks the '16:8 window' fast type, capture the fast-start timestamp and show a calm circular progress ring (reuse the existing teal ring vocabulary) with 'Xh Ym fasted', the eating-window open time, and a state label (Fasting / Eating window open). Client-side only, NO backend: persist fastStart + window config in localStorage keyed by date; the ring updates from a 1-min interval; the existing 'End fast' button clears it. Skip push reminders and fast history in v1. EFFORT: roughly 1-2 days frontend, no backend, no schema -- extends the fasting toggle already on Nutrition.

issues.description: [suggestion] Auto-generate a weekly grocery list from the assigned diet plan. USER PROBLEM: users get a 7-day plan (DietPlanWeek) but must manually work out what to buy to actually cook it — adherence dies at the grocery store, the biggest gap between having a plan and following it. EVIDENCE: the backend already serves per-ingredient data (name + quantity + unit) for every meal (RecipeDetail consumes recipe.ingredients); DietPlanWeek already loads the whole week. A grep shows zero existing grocery/shopping code, so this is a genuine gap. Comparable trackers (Mealime, Eat This Much, PlateJoy) ship auto grocery lists as a headline retention feature. V1 SCOPE: new route /diet-plan/shopping-list reached from a 'Shopping list' button on DietPlanWeek. Client-side only, NO backend change: flatten ingredients across the week's assigned meals, sum duplicates by normalised name+unit, sort alphabetically (skip a category taxonomy in v1), render a check-off list with checked state persisted in localStorage. Add one 'Copy as text / Share' button (WhatsApp-heavy India audience) so the list can be sent to whoever shops. EFFORT: roughly 1-2 days frontend, no backend, no schema. Reuses the existing diet-plan query and ingredient shape.
